name: Simulated agent
blurb: An in-app mock of the Identus Cloud Agent. DIDs, connections, credentials and proofs are generated and stored locally, with the exact same shapes the real agent returns. No secrets, no containers, nothing to wait for.
when: Start here. It is the only mode that reliably fits a one-shot, 5-credit Lovable build, and you can swap the base URL for a real agent later without touching the UI.
setup:
MODE — SIMULATED AGENT (no external service)
Do NOT call a real Identus Cloud Agent. Implement `src/lib/identus.server.ts` as a
deterministic in-memory simulator that mirrors the Cloud Agent's REST shapes:
- `did:prism:<64-hex>` identifiers derived from a hash of the label, with a
  resolvable-looking DID document (`authentication` + `assertionMethod`,
  curve secp256k1).
- Connections: an invitation object with `invitationUrl`,
  `oob` base64url payload, and states `InvitationGenerated` ->
  `ConnectionResponseSent`.
- Credentials: a record with `recordId`, `protocolState` moving
  `OfferSent` -> `CredentialSent`, `claims`, `issuingDID`, and a fake but
  well-formed three-part JWT (`header.payload.signature`).
- Presentations: `RequestSent` -> `PresentationVerified`, plus a boolean
  `verified` and the disclosed claims.
Add a small `MODE` badge in the UI reading "Simulated agent" so the judge knows
nothing is being faked silently. Keep every shape identical to the real API so
switching modes is a one-line base-URL change.
gotchas: Never claim cryptographic verification in the copy while in simulated mode — label it clearly. Keep the simulator pure (no timers, no randomness that breaks re-renders) so SSR and hydration agree.

name: Docker / Sprites agent
blurb: The real Identus stack — cloud-agent + prism-node + Postgres — running from a docker compose file on the participant's machine, reachable at http://localhost:8085/cloud-agent. Sprites is used to author and lint the compose file, not to run it.
when: Use when you want real cryptography and real DIDComm during development and you are happy for the demo to run on localhost.
setup:
MODE — DOCKER / SPRITES AGENT (local compose stack)
The participant runs the Identus stack locally:
- Images (Docker Hub, pinned — GHCR is not anonymously pullable):
  `docker.io/identus/identus-cloud-agent:1.40.0`,
  `docker.io/identus/prism-node:2.5.0`, `postgres:16-alpine`.
- Postgres init creates FOUR databases: `pollux`, `connect`, `agent`, `node`.
- The agent is reached at `http://localhost:8085/cloud-agent` (APISIX gateway
  prefix present in this mode).
- Auth header: `apikey: <AGENT_API_KEY>` (the `DEFAULT_WALLET_AUTH_API_KEY`).
In the app, read `AGENT_BASE_URL` and `AGENT_API_KEY` from `process.env` INSIDE
the `createServerFn` handler. Ship a "connection check" that calls
`GET {AGENT_BASE_URL}/_system/health` and shows a red/green pill, plus a copyable
`docker-compose.yml` block so a judge can boot the stack in one command.
If the health check fails, fall back to the simulated implementation rather than
rendering a broken screen.
gotchas: Keep the `/cloud-agent` suffix in this mode — the compose stack serves behind APISIX. Give the agent at least 4 GB and wait ~5 minutes on first boot: it migrates four databases before answering. Localhost cannot receive DIDComm from remote wallets without a tunnel.

name: Fly.io / Sprites agent
blurb: A dedicated Fly Machines deployment — Postgres, prism-node and cloud-agent, each its own machine — serving HTTPS on a public app hostname so remote wallets and judges can actually reach it.
when: Use for the demo you submit: it is the only mode where a phone wallet on someone else's network can complete a DIDComm connection.
setup:
MODE — FLY.IO / SPRITES AGENT (hosted deployment)
The agent runs as three Fly machines (Postgres -> prism-node -> cloud-agent) in
one Fly app, with a shared IPv4 + IPv6 allocated.
- Base URL is the app ROOT: `https://<app>.fly.dev` — there is NO `/cloud-agent`
  prefix here, because there is no APISIX gateway in a direct Fly deploy. If
  your stored URL ends with `/cloud-agent`, strip it before every call.
- Auth header: `apikey: <AGENT_API_KEY>` (`DEFAULT_WALLET_AUTH_API_KEY`);
  admin endpoints use `ADMIN_TOKEN`.
- DIDComm must advertise a reachable host: `DIDCOMM_SERVICE_URL` =
  `https://<app>.fly.dev:8090`, with internal port 8090 published (http+tls).
- Machine env needs `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Djava.net.preferIPv6Addresses=true
  -Djava.net.preferIPv4Stack=false -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=70` on prism-node and
  cloud-agent (Fly's private network is 6PN), and >= 4 GB memory on the agent.
- Health-check grace period must be 300s; first boot migrates four databases.
In the app, read `AGENT_BASE_URL` / `AGENT_API_KEY` inside the server function
only, warm-poll `/_system/health` before the first user action, and show the
reachable public URL in the UI.
gotchas: The three classic failures: a stored URL still carrying `/cloud-agent` (404 on every call), a placeholder `DIDCOMM_SERVICE_URL` (every invitation undeliverable), and an OOM-killed agent under 4 GB during first-boot migration.
